params.body:
**Triage proposal** (from the forwarded mail; change the labels if it is wrong)
Category: request  Priority: P2
Summary: Trendwolves editorial sent a revised version (20 October 2026) of the document "Gentells Standard: Who, What and Why" and asks for it to be integrated. The standard carries the 5 October version (0.8.0); the new one widens it from two axes to four and changes several tagging rules.

What the new version changes compared with the standard on main (0.12.0):

- **Millennials** (born 1980 to 1994) become a tagged generation, as context only: always alongside Gen Z, Gen Alpha or Young Families, never alone. Until now `rules/cohort.json` said they are not tagged.
- **Gen Beta** (2025 to 2039) goes from reserved to tagged, and a Gen Beta signal always carries Young Families too.
- **Elements**: a thirteenth element, **Codes** (slang, jargon, greetings, emoji, memes as language), and sharper descriptions for the twelve. A weight under 0.3 is not tagged, and the element with the highest weight is the main element. The closed list of thirteen leaves out Gaming, which is `proposed` in the standard.
- **Needs (drivers)** become an axis on signals, not only on trends: exactly one main need and at most one secondary, chosen with a test question (what does this young person lose if it fails?). Each need gets a definition and what is lost when it fails; the frame is self-determination theory plus security, status and meaning.
- **Element against need**: a boundary table (gathering is not belonging, success is not status, and so on). A need is never derived from an element.
- **Combinations**: the smallest reading unit is main element × main need (78 cells), always read as a share of the period's signals, and only counted from 5 signals from at least 3 sources. Five reading movements are named.
- **Tagging rules**: Gen Z or Gen Alpha is central on every signal (or Young Families); a European lens for what enters the Observatory.
- The document writes tags as `el-*`, `drv-*` and `gen-genalpha`; the standard keeps its ids and takes those as hidden labels, as it did in 0.8.0.

What it touches after the standard: the pipeline's classifier (needs per signal, Codes, the 0.3 floor, Millennials and Gen Beta) once a release is tagged and synced.

Source: Portal mail:23 (the document itself stays there).
params.title: Adopt the 20 October 2026 version of Who, What and Why
